finding: The focus adjective حَمِئَة describes the spring, while حَمَإٍ مَّسْنُونٍ names the material of human creation in one repeated creation episode. Because a قَوْمًا is found at this spring, its muddy setting could bring human origin into the scene; the three occurrences in 15:26, 15:28, and 15:33 repeat that one episode rather than provide three separate settings.

evidence.ar: فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍۢ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًۭا
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ مِن صَلْصَٰلٍۢ مِّنْ حَمَإٍۢ مَّسْنُونٍۢ
وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى خَٰلِقٌۢ بَشَرًۭا مِّن صَلْصَٰلٍۢ مِّنْ حَمَإٍۢ مَّسْنُونٍۢ
قَالَ لَمْ أَكُن لِّأَسْجُدَ لِبَشَرٍ خَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن صَلْصَٰلٍۢ مِّنْ حَمَإٍۢ مَّسْنُونٍۢ

missing: The focus does not mention creation or equate this spring’s mud with the creation material, and حَمِئَة and حَمَإ are different forms. Dictionary evidence that the adjective names the same specific substance, or another creation cue in the scene, could establish whether the origin echo is activated.

finding: Across the journey, قَوْم recurs as a scene-role at three distinct stops: a people at sunset, a people exposed to sunrise without a screen, and a people between the barriers who ask for help against Gog and Magog. This places the focus group within a route-wide pattern of encountering different populations, while the people and their circumstances remain distinct.

evidence.ar: وَجَدَهَا تَطْلُعُ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍۢ لَّمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُم مِّن دُونِهَا سِتْرًۭا
وَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمَا قَوْمًۭا لَّا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلًۭا
قَالُوا۟ يَٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِنَّ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ مُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَهَلْ نَجْعَلُ لَكَ خَرْجًا عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَجْعَلَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمْ سَدًّۭا

activation: The same traveler’s repeated reaching and finding frames these populations along the west-to-east journey; the later group’s direct request makes the varied encounters explicit.
limits: The repeated noun does not establish that the groups are the same people or that they receive the same treatment.

finding: Qur’anic قَرْن can name a past people or age: 6:6 describes a قَرْن empowered in the land and later destroyed for its deeds. Surah 18 uses the matching empowerment-in-the-land wording for the bearer of the title ذُو ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ, who in the focus ayah is authorized to decide how to treat a newly encountered people. The shared root and scene frame his rule against the memory of empowered past communities.

evidence.ar: أَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍۢ مَّكَّنَّٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مَا لَمْ نُمَكِّن لَّكُمْ وَأَرْسَلْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيْهِم مِّدْرَارًۭا وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرَ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهِمْ فَأَهْلَكْنَٰهُم بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَأَنشَأْنَا مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ قَرْنًا ءَاخَرِينَ
قُلْنَا يَٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًۭا

activation: The focus applies the dual title to a ruler whose land-empowerment has just been stated, while the people he finds become the subject of a decision about justice and good treatment.
limits: The past-generation noun and the definite dual title are distinct forms; this parallel does not establish that ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ means “two generations,” or that the ruler shares the earlier communities’ fate.

finding: The focus places punishment as a direct option entrusted to Dhul-Qarnayn: the second-person تُعَذِّبَ is taken up in 18:87 as his نُعَذِّبُهُۥ, followed by a separate divine فَيُعَذِّبُهُۥ when the wrongdoer returns to his Lord. The Qur’an also describes Allah punishing through human hands, giving a parallel for human action within divine authority.

evidence.ar: إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًۭا
قَالَ أَمَّا مَن ظَلَمَ فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُۥ ثُمَّ يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ فَيُعَذِّبُهُۥ عَذَابًۭا نُّكْرًۭا
قَٰتِلُوهُمْ يُعَذِّبْهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ وَيُخْزِهِمْ وَيَنصُرْكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ

activation: قُلْنَا introduces the direct address, and the immediate continuation limits the first punishment to مَن ظَلَمَ before describing the person’s return to God.
limits: The passage distinguishes the ruler’s punishment from the later divine one, but does not specify the first punishment’s method or duration; 9:14 does not settle how the authority in this scene is exercised.
